# stamity

> An ESM-only TypeScript CLI that generates agentic coding setups — a charter, commands,
> agents, skills, rules, hooks and MCP wiring — for four AI coding clients from one
> canonical source model.

Every path below is relative to the repository root, and every page is markdown. A page
rendered from code names the command that rewrites it — there is more than one generator
here — and the test suite byte-compares each against a fresh render, so a page that lags
its generator fails a check instead of reading as current. An entry naming no command is
hand-written or corpus source. Nothing here links outside this tree.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what stamity generates from one canonical source and for which clients, the nine verbs, where each subject lives, and what this repository can prove.
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): the contributor gate CI runs, the three test lanes, the regeneration command for every derived file, and what a pull request has to pass.
- [Security](SECURITY.md): what the engine defends today, what it does not defend, and where to send a vulnerability report.
- [Governance](GOVERNANCE.md): who decides, the two required checks a change passes to land, what the private layer holds, and what happens if the maintainer stops.
- [Code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md): the behaviour expected here, the two channels a report goes through, and the enforcement ladder.

## Guides

- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): setting stamity up in a repository for the first time — what init asks and writes per client, where state lives, and one change proved by a passing verification gate.
- [Working with stamity](docs/working-with-stamity.md): which of the nine touchpoints to open, what that one may do, what is on disk when it stops, and how to run two changes at once.
- [Doctrine](docs/doctrine.md): why stamity ships what it ships — the root question every artifact answers, the four pillars and their public enforcement surfaces, and how an artifact is deleted.
- [Customization](docs/customization.md): making the shipped agents, rules, commands and skills say what a repository needs — where an override lives, the one save gate, patching instead of replacing, removal, and the fork layer below it.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): the exit model, every check row and its remedy, the common failures, and where to report one.
- [Workspaces](docs/workspaces.md): one policy across several repositories — what a workspace is, the manifest, the two ways to create one, the status rows, and what the cascade pushes down.
- [Packs and trust](docs/packs-and-trust.md): what a pack is, the four-rung trust ladder, what a verified signature does and does not prove, signing one of your own, the org policy, and how to remove a pack.
- [Enterprise forks](docs/enterprise-forks.md): taking the next upstream release into a customized fork — the lane's config and verbs, conflicts, the gates that decide, landing, the fork layer, and the opt-in workflow.
- [Security mapping](docs/security-mapping.md): the version-pinned crosswalk from this repository's own controls to the OWASP agentic, LLM and web lists, the joint guidance and the NIST AI RMF — seven surfaces, their residuals, and the gaps.
- [Migration](docs/migration.md): moving a repository off the predecessor setup — the in-place path, the uninstall-first path, what transfers, and the removal left to you.

## Generated reference

- [CLI reference](docs/cli-reference.md): every command, argument, flag and exit status, rendered from the program itself. Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-docs.mjs`.
- [Configuration reference](docs/configuration.md): every addressable config key, what it accepts, and what binds when it is unset. Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-docs.mjs`.
- [Measurements](docs/measurements.md): the verified merge-ready rate over this repository's own run records, the npm reach proxy, the eval run of record, and the first-run proof lanes. Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-docs.mjs`.
- [Client capability matrix](docs/capability-matrix.md): what each supported client can do, rendered from the adapters' declared dialect facts. Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-capability-matrix.mjs`.

## Content corpus

- [Agents](docs/reference/agents.md): every agent in the corpus — its trigger, tags, load mode and retirement condition. Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-docs.mjs`.
- [Skills](docs/reference/skills.md): every skill in the corpus — its trigger, tags, load mode and retirement condition. Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-docs.mjs`.
- [Rules](docs/reference/rules.md): every rule in the corpus — its trigger, tags, load mode and retirement condition. Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-docs.mjs`.
- [Commands](docs/reference/commands.md): every command in the corpus — its trigger, tags, load mode and retirement condition. Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-docs.mjs`.
- [Packs](docs/reference/packs.md): the first-party packs `add` can install, and what each one ships. Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-docs.mjs`.
- [MCP servers](docs/reference/mcp-servers.md): every curated MCP server id `mcp.servers` accepts, with its pin, credentials and blast radius. Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-docs.mjs`.
- [Charter](content/charter/stamity-charter.md): the always-on context every generated setup carries: repo facts, floor invariants, touchpoint index.
